title: Number of Islands
key_pattern: DFS/BFS flood fill
key_insight: Each island is one connected component; flood-filling it marks every cell so it is counted exactly once.
statement: Count islands of '1's connected horizontally or vertically in a grid.
edge_cases: Empty grid
recursion depth on a huge island
google_follow_up: What if land is added one cell at a time (Number of Islands II, union-find)?

title: Course Schedule
key_pattern: Cycle detection (Kahn or 3-colour DFS)
key_insight: All courses can be finished exactly when the prerequisite graph has no directed cycle.
statement: Decide if all courses can be finished given prerequisite pairs.
edge_cases: Self-dependency
disconnected components
google_follow_up: Return the minimum number of semesters needed.

title: Rotting Oranges
key_pattern: Multi-source BFS
key_insight: Start BFS from every rotten orange at once; the number of BFS levels is the minutes elapsed.
statement: Return minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if impossible.
edge_cases: No fresh oranges at all returns 0
google_follow_up: What if rot spreads with different speeds per cell?

title: Number of Provinces
key_pattern: Union-find (or DFS) over the adjacency matrix
key_insight: Provinces are connected components; every union of two separate groups lowers the count by one.
statement: Given an n x n matrix of direct connections between cities, count the groups of connected cities.
edge_cases: Diagonal self-connections
an isolated city is its own province
google_follow_up: What if connections are added and removed over time?

title: Clone Graph
key_pattern: DFS/BFS with an original -> copy hash map
key_insight: Store each node's copy before visiting its neighbours, so cycles reuse the copy instead of looping.
statement: Return a deep copy of a connected undirected graph, given a reference to one of its nodes.
edge_cases: Cycles: reuse the existing copy instead of recursing forever
Empty graph (null node)
google_follow_up: Replicate the graph across machines where nodes are sharded by id.

title: Course Schedule II
key_pattern: Topological sort (Kahn's algorithm)
key_insight: Repeatedly take a course with no remaining prerequisites; the order you remove them is a valid schedule.
statement: Return an order in which to take all courses, or empty if impossible.
edge_cases: Cycle detection: output shorter than V
google_follow_up: What if prerequisites change frequently?

title: Word Ladder
key_pattern: BFS over wildcard pattern buckets
key_insight: Words are nodes and one-letter edits are edges; BFS gives the fewest steps, and wildcard buckets (h*t) find neighbours fast.
statement: Find the shortest transformation length from begin to end word, changing one letter at a time via a word list.
edge_cases: End word missing from the list
google_follow_up: Bidirectional BFS: why is it faster?

title: Alien Dictionary
key_pattern: Build edges from adjacent words, topological sort
key_insight: Only the first differing character of two adjacent words gives an ordering edge; a topological sort of those edges is the alphabet.
statement: Given words sorted in an unknown alphabet, derive a valid order of its letters.
edge_cases: Prefix case like ['abc', 'ab'] is invalid
google_follow_up: Return all valid orders, or detect if the order is unique.

title: Network Delay Time
key_pattern: Dijkstra with a min-heap
key_insight: Everyone has the signal at the largest shortest-path distance from the source.
statement: Find how long it takes a signal from node k to reach all nodes, or -1.
edge_cases: Unreachable nodes
stale heap entries
google_follow_up: What if edge weights can be negative?

title: Accounts Merge
key_pattern: Union-find on emails
key_insight: Emails are the shared keys: union every email in an account, and each root's group is one person.
statement: Merge accounts that share at least one email address.
edge_cases: Same name does not imply the same person
google_follow_up: What if accounts live in shards across data centres?

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
key_pattern: DFS + memoisation (DAG longest path)
key_insight: Strictly increasing moves form a DAG, so each cell's best path is computed once and memoised.
statement: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing path in a matrix (4 directions).
edge_cases: Equal neighbours are not increasing
google_follow_up: Return the path itself; solve with topological order instead of recursion.

title: Minimum Height Trees
key_pattern: Topological peeling: trim leaves layer by layer
key_insight: The best roots are the tree's centres; peeling leaves layer by layer leaves the 1 or 2 centre nodes.
statement: Given a tree of n nodes as an edge list, return every node that, chosen as the root, gives the tree its minimum height.
edge_cases: n == 1 returns [0]
the answer always has 1 or 2 nodes
google_follow_up: Edges are added one at a time: keep the answer updated without recomputing.

title: Path With Minimum Effort
key_pattern: Dijkstra with a min-heap where path cost is the largest step so far
key_insight: Dijkstra still works when a path costs its largest step, because that cost never decreases along a path.
statement: In a grid of heights, find a path from top-left to bottom-right that minimises the largest absolute height difference between neighbouring cells on the path.
edge_cases: A 1 x 1 grid needs 0 effort
relax with max(), not +
google_follow_up: The grid is 10^5 x 10^5 and stored as tiles on disk: how do you search it?

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
key_pattern: Reverse flood fill uphill from each ocean's border
key_insight: Flip the direction: flood uphill from each ocean's border; cells reached from both oceans are the answer.
statement: Water flows to neighbouring cells of equal or lower height. Return every cell from which water can reach both the Pacific (top/left edges) and the Atlantic (bottom/right edges).
edge_cases: Border cells already touch an ocean
Equal heights let water flow both ways
google_follow_up: Sensors update heights continuously: keep the answer fresh without a full recompute.

title: Making A Large Island
key_pattern: Label each island with its size, then try flipping every 0
key_insight: Label each island with its size once; then each 0 gives 1 + the sizes of its distinct neighbouring islands.
statement: In an n x n binary grid you may change at most one 0 into a 1. Return the size of the largest island you can get.
edge_cases: A grid of all 1s returns n * n
Count a neighbouring island once even if it touches the 0 on two sides
google_follow_up: You may flip up to K cells.

title: Sequence Reconstruction
key_pattern: Kahn's algorithm with a unique-choice check
key_insight: The order is unique exactly when Kahn's algorithm never has two courses available at the same time.
statement: Given a permutation nums and a list of subsequences, decide whether nums is the only shortest sequence that contains every subsequence.
edge_cases: More than one zero in-degree node at any step means the order is not unique
Values outside 1..n inside the subsequences
google_follow_up: Subsequences arrive as a stream of execution logs: detect the moment the order becomes unique.

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
key_pattern: Bellman-Ford limited to K+1 rounds (or BFS by stops)
key_insight: Allow at most K + 1 rounds of relaxation and copy distances per round so no path uses extra edges.
statement: Find the cheapest price from src to dst with at most k stops.
edge_cases: Copy distances per round to avoid using more stops
google_follow_up: Why does plain Dijkstra fail with the stop limit?

title: Evaluate Division
key_pattern: Weighted graph BFS/DFS or weighted union-find
key_insight: a / b = 2 is an edge a -> b weighted 2 and b -> a weighted 1/2; a query is the product of weights along a path.
statement: Given equations like a/b = 2.0, answer queries such as a/c.
edge_cases: Unknown variables
x/x for a known x is 1.0
google_follow_up: Answer 10^6 queries quickly (weighted union-find with path compression).

title: Bus Routes
key_pattern: BFS where nodes are bus routes (stop -> routes index)
key_insight: Search over buses, not stops: each BFS level is one more bus taken.
statement: Given bus routes as lists of stops, return the fewest buses needed to travel from a source stop to a target stop, or -1.
edge_cases: source == target needs 0 buses
visit each route only once
google_follow_up: What if you must minimise total travel time with a penalty per transfer?

title: Swim in Rising Water
key_pattern: Min-heap Dijkstra on the highest elevation along the path (or union-find by time)
key_insight: The answer is the smallest possible highest cell on a path: Dijkstra on max(), or add cells by height until start and end connect.
statement: In an n x n grid of distinct elevations, the water level rises by one each second. Find the earliest time you can swim from the top-left to the bottom-right cell.
edge_cases: The start and end cell elevations already bound the answer from below
google_follow_up: Answer the earliest time for 10^5 different (source, target) pairs.

title: Second Minimum Time to Reach Destination
key_pattern: BFS keeping the two smallest distinct edge counts per node
key_insight: All edges cost the same, so find the second-smallest edge count with BFS that keeps two distinct visits per node, then convert it to time with signal waits.
statement: Every edge of a city graph takes `time` minutes and every node has a signal that flips green/red every `change` minutes (you may only leave on green). Return the second smallest time to get from node 1 to node n.
edge_cases: The second minimum must be strictly larger than the minimum
Arriving exactly when the signal turns red means waiting a full red phase
google_follow_up: Edges now have different travel times: what replaces BFS?

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
key_pattern: Hierholzer's Eulerian path with lexically ordered destinations
key_insight: Using every ticket once is an Eulerian path: DFS to the smallest destination first, append airports on the way back, then reverse.
statement: Given airline tickets [from, to], rebuild the itinerary that starts at JFK, uses every ticket exactly once and is lexically smallest.
edge_cases: A dead-end destination must be appended last (post-order), not visited first
Duplicate tickets between the same two airports
google_follow_up: 10^7 tickets are sharded across data centres: how do you validate the itinerary?

title: Word Ladder II
key_pattern: BFS layer by layer building a parent map, then backtrack every path
key_insight: BFS keeps only shortest-path parent links; backtracking from the end through those links lists every shortest path.
statement: Return all shortest transformation sequences from beginWord to endWord, changing one letter at a time using only words from a list.
edge_cases: Remove a level's words only after the whole level ends, or equal-length paths are lost
endWord missing from the list returns []
google_follow_up: The number of shortest paths explodes: stream them lazily instead of building the list.

title: Critical Connections in a Network
key_pattern: Tarjan's bridges: discovery time + low-link
key_insight: An edge is critical when the child cannot reach the parent or anything earlier without it: low[child] > disc[parent].
statement: Servers form an undirected network. Return every connection whose removal would leave some servers unable to reach others.
edge_cases: Skip only the edge you came from, not every edge to the parent
10^5 servers overflow the recursion stack: use an iterative DFS
google_follow_up: Links fail and recover in real time: maintain the set of critical links.

title: Number of Islands II
key_pattern: Online union-find on added land cells
key_insight: Each new land cell adds an island and every successful union with a neighbouring island removes one.
statement: Cells of an all-water grid are turned into land one at a time. After each addition, return the number of islands.
edge_cases: Adding the same cell twice must not change the count
Union with each distinct neighbouring island only once
google_follow_up: Cells can also turn back into water: why does union-find break, and what replaces it?

title: Find the Safest Path in a Grid
key_pattern: Multi-source BFS for safeness, then a max-min path (Dijkstra or binary search + BFS)
key_insight: First compute every cell's distance to the nearest thief with one multi-source BFS, then maximise the minimum along a path.
statement: Thieves sit on some cells of an n x n grid. A path's safeness is the smallest Manhattan distance from any path cell to any thief. Return the maximum safeness of a path from top-left to bottom-right.
edge_cases: A thief on the start or end cell makes the answer 0
Safeness is a bottleneck (minimum along the path), not a sum
google_follow_up: Thieves move every second: update the safest path incrementally.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
key_pattern: Post-order: return the node found in each subtree
key_insight: Post-order: the first node that finds p in one subtree and q in the other (or is one of them) is the answer.
statement: Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary tree.
edge_cases: One node is an ancestor of the other
google_follow_up: What if nodes have parent pointers? What if p or q may be missing?

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
key_pattern: DFS with (low, high) bounds or in-order
key_insight: Every node must sit inside the (low, high) range set by all its ancestors, not just its parent.
statement: Decide whether a binary tree is a valid binary search tree.
edge_cases: Duplicates
values at integer limits
google_follow_up: Do it iteratively with O(1) extra space (Morris traversal).

title: Binary Tree Right Side View
key_pattern: BFS level order, take the last node per level
key_insight: The visible node is the last one on each BFS level.
statement: Return the values visible when looking at a binary tree from the right side.
edge_cases: Left subtree deeper than the right one
google_follow_up: Return both the left and right views in one pass.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
key_pattern: In-order traversal with counter
key_insight: In-order traversal of a BST visits values in sorted order; stop at the k-th.
statement: Return the k-th smallest value in a binary search tree.
edge_cases: k equal to the number of nodes
google_follow_up: What if the BST is modified often and you query often?

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
key_pattern: DFS height, update global left + right
key_insight: The longest path through a node is its left height + right height; take the maximum over all nodes.
statement: Return the length of the longest path between any two nodes in a binary tree.
edge_cases: Path need not pass through the root
google_follow_up: Solve the same for an n-ary tree.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
key_pattern: Trie nodes with children map + end flag
key_insight: Words that share a prefix share nodes, so each operation costs the word's length, not the dictionary's size.
statement: Implement insert, search and startsWith for a prefix tree.
edge_cases: Prefix that is also a full word
google_follow_up: Add delete; compress the trie (radix tree).

title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
key_pattern: BFS by level, reverse every other level (or fill a deque from alternating ends)
key_insight: It is ordinary level-order traversal; only the output direction flips per level.
statement: Return the level-order values of a binary tree, alternating left-to-right and right-to-left on each level.
edge_cases: Empty tree returns []
do not reverse the BFS queue itself, only the level output
google_follow_up: Stream each level to a client as soon as it is complete, with memory bounded by one level.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
key_pattern: Pre-order with null markers
key_insight: Pre-order with explicit null markers fixes the tree's shape, so one pass rebuilds it.
statement: Design encode/decode functions that turn a binary tree into a string and back.
edge_cases: Negative and multi-digit values
empty tree
google_follow_up: How would you make the encoding compact for a near-complete tree?

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
key_pattern: DFS returning best downward gain, update global
key_insight: Return the best single downward branch (dropping negatives) to the parent; update the global answer with left + node + right.
statement: Find the maximum sum of any path between two nodes in a binary tree.
edge_cases: All negative values: answer is the largest single node
google_follow_up: Return the path itself, not just the sum.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
key_pattern: Recursion with inorder index map
key_insight: Pre-order's first value is the root; its position in the in-order list splits the left and right subtrees.
statement: Rebuild a binary tree given its pre-order and in-order traversals.
edge_cases: Skewed tree causing deep recursion
google_follow_up: Why can pre-order + post-order not uniquely rebuild a tree?

title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
key_pattern: Convert to graph (parent map) + BFS
key_insight: Add parent links so the tree becomes an undirected graph, then BFS k steps from the target.
statement: Return all nodes exactly distance k from a target node.
edge_cases: k == 0 returns the target itself
google_follow_up: Answer many (target, k) queries efficiently.

title: Word Search II
key_pattern: Trie + backtracking DFS with pruning
key_insight: Put every word in a trie so one board DFS checks all words at once and stops on dead prefixes.
statement: Find all dictionary words that can be formed by adjacent letters in a board.
edge_cases: Same word found twice
remove found words from the trie
google_follow_up: What if the dictionary has 10^6 words and the board is huge?

title: Kth Ancestor of a Tree Node
key_pattern: Binary lifting: precompute every node's 2^j-th ancestor
key_insight: Store each node's 2^j-th ancestor; a k-th ancestor is one jump per set bit of k.
time_target: O(N log N) build, O(log k) query
statement: A tree is given as a parent[] array. Design getKthAncestor(node, k) that returns the k-th ancestor of node, or -1.
edge_cases: k larger than the node's depth returns -1
The root's parent is -1: stop jumping there
google_follow_up: Reuse the lifting table to answer lowest-common-ancestor queries in O(log N).

title: Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
key_pattern: DFS with (col, row, val) then sort
key_insight: Record (column, row, value) for every node, then sort; ties at the same spot sort by value.
statement: Return node values grouped by column, sorted by row then value within a column.
edge_cases: Two nodes at the same row and column: sort by value
google_follow_up: How would you avoid the global sort?

title: Design Search Autocomplete System
key_pattern: Trie of sentences with counts; top 3 by (count desc, text asc)
key_insight: Keep a trie node per prefix with sentence counts; each typed character moves one node deeper and returns its top 3.
time_target: O(L) per character with cached top-3
statement: As a user types each character, return the 3 most frequent past sentences that start with the current prefix. '#' ends the sentence and records it.
edge_cases: Ties in frequency sort by ASCII order
After '#', reset the prefix and add 1 to that sentence's count
google_follow_up: Serve 10^5 QPS across regions: what can be cached, and how stale may it be?

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
key_pattern: Min-heap of list heads
key_insight: Only the current head of each list can be next, so a heap of k heads finds it in O(log k).
statement: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
edge_cases: Some lists empty
google_follow_up: What if each list lives on a different machine and memory is 64MB?

title: Top K Frequent Elements
key_pattern: Count + size-K min-heap (or bucket sort)
key_insight: Count, then keep a size-k min-heap so the least frequent of the current top k is evicted first.
statement: Return the k most frequent elements.
edge_cases: Ties in frequency
k equal to the number of distinct values
google_follow_up: What if the input is a stream of 10^9 events (heavy hitters / count-min sketch)?

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
key_pattern: Size-K min-heap or quickselect
key_insight: A size-k min-heap holds the k largest values seen; its top is the k-th largest.
statement: Return the k-th largest element in an unsorted array.
edge_cases: Duplicates count separately
google_follow_up: Average vs. worst case of quickselect; how to defend against the worst case?

title: Car Pooling
key_pattern: Sort by pickup + min-heap of drop-offs (or difference array)
key_insight: Load only changes at pick-ups and drop-offs; process those events in order and check the running total.
statement: A car with a fixed capacity only drives east. Given trips [passengers, from, to], decide if it can complete every trip without exceeding capacity.
edge_cases: Drop-offs at a location happen before pick-ups at the same location
google_follow_up: What if locations go up to 10^9 and trips arrive as a stream?

title: Find Median from Data Stream
key_pattern: Two heaps: max-heap low half, min-heap high half
key_insight: A max-heap holds the smaller half and a min-heap the larger half; with sizes within one, the median is at the tops.
statement: Design a structure that supports adding numbers and returning the running median.
edge_cases: Even count returns the average of the two middles
google_follow_up: What if 99% of numbers are in [0,100]?

title: Task Scheduler
key_pattern: Greedy by max frequency (formula or heap)
key_insight: The most frequent task sets the frame: (maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + tasks tied at maxFreq, or the task count if larger.
statement: Find the minimum time units to run tasks when identical tasks need n idle units between them.
edge_cases: several tasks share the max frequency
google_follow_up: Return the actual schedule, not just its length.

title: Single-Threaded CPU
key_pattern: Sort by enqueue time; min-heap of (processing time, index); simulate the clock
key_insight: Simulate the clock: push every task that has arrived, run the shortest, and jump ahead when nothing is waiting.
statement: Each task has an enqueue time and a processing time. A single CPU always runs the shortest available task (ties by index). Return the order tasks are processed.
edge_cases: When the CPU is idle and the heap is empty, jump the clock to the next enqueue time
google_follow_up: Now there are K CPUs and tasks carry priorities: what changes?

title: Merge Intervals
key_pattern: Sort by start, merge overlaps
key_insight: After sorting by start, an interval can only overlap the last merged one, so one pass merges everything.
statement: Merge all overlapping intervals and return the non-overlapping result.
edge_cases: Touching intervals like [1,4] and [4,5] should merge
google_follow_up: What if intervals arrive one by one and you must keep the merged set?

title: Insert Interval
key_pattern: Three-phase scan: before, overlap, after
key_insight: Intervals ending before the new one stay, overlapping ones merge into it, and the rest follow.
statement: Insert a new interval into a sorted list of non-overlapping intervals, merging if needed.
edge_cases: New interval before all or after all existing intervals
google_follow_up: Do it with binary search when the list is huge.

title: Meeting Rooms II
key_pattern: Min-heap of end times or sweep line
key_insight: Rooms needed = the most meetings running at the same moment; sweep starts and ends in time order.
statement: Given meeting time intervals, find the minimum number of conference rooms required.
edge_cases: A meeting ending exactly when another starts frees the room
google_follow_up: What if you must also return which room each meeting uses?

title: Employee Free Time
key_pattern: Merge sorted interval lists with a heap
key_insight: Merge everyone's busy time into one sorted timeline; the gaps are the common free time.
statement: Given each employee's sorted working intervals, return the finite common free time slots.
edge_cases: Ignore infinite gaps before the first and after the last interval
google_follow_up: What if schedules live in different time zones and services?

title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
key_pattern: Sort by end + DP with binary search
key_insight: Sort by end time; best = max(skip this job, take it + best before its start), found by binary search.
statement: Choose non-overlapping jobs (start, end, profit) to maximise total profit.
edge_cases: A job may start exactly when another ends
google_follow_up: What if you have K machines instead of one?

title: Meeting Rooms III
key_pattern: Sort by start; min-heap of free room ids + min-heap of (end, room)
key_insight: Track free rooms by number and busy rooms by (end, number); a delayed meeting takes the earliest-freeing room and keeps its length.
time_target: O(M log M + M log N)
statement: n rooms are numbered 0..n-1. Each meeting [start, end) goes to the lowest-numbered free room, or waits for the earliest room to free up and keeps its duration. Return the room that hosted the most meetings.
edge_cases: A delayed meeting keeps its original duration
ties on end time go to the lowest room id
google_follow_up: What if rooms have different capacities and meetings have sizes?

title: House Robber
key_pattern: 1D DP: rob or skip
key_insight: best[i] = max(best[i - 1], best[i - 2] + nums[i]): skip this house or rob it.
statement: Maximise money robbed from houses in a line without robbing two adjacent houses.
edge_cases: Single house
google_follow_up: Houses in a circle (House Robber II) or a tree (III).

title: Unique Paths
key_pattern: Grid DP (or combinatorics)
key_insight: Paths into a cell = paths from above + paths from the left.
statement: Count the paths from top-left to bottom-right moving only right or down.
edge_cases: 1 x N grid has exactly one path
google_follow_up: Add obstacles; what if the grid is 10^5 x 10^5?

title: Decode Ways
key_pattern: 1D DP with one- and two-digit lookback
key_insight: ways[i] = ways[i - 1] if the last digit is valid + ways[i - 2] if the last two digits are 10-26.
statement: Count how many ways a digit string can be decoded where 'A'=1 ... 'Z'=26.
edge_cases: Zeros: '0', '06', '100' have no valid decoding
google_follow_up: Add a '*' wildcard digit (Decode Ways II).

title: Word Break
key_pattern: DP over prefixes with a word set
key_insight: ok[i] is true when some dictionary word ends at i and ok is true where that word starts.
statement: Decide if a string can be split into a sequence of dictionary words.
edge_cases: Reusing words is allowed
google_follow_up: Return all sentences (Word Break II); what blows up?

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
key_pattern: Expand around each of the 2N - 1 centres (interval DP also works)
key_insight: Every palindrome mirrors around a centre; expanding from each of the 2n - 1 centres checks them all.
statement: Return the longest substring of s that reads the same forwards and backwards.
edge_cases: Even-length palindromes need a centre between two characters
google_follow_up: How does Manacher's algorithm bring this down to O(N)?

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
key_pattern: 0/1 knapsack over reachable sums (loop sums downwards)
key_insight: It is subset-sum to total / 2: track reachable sums, using each number once.
statement: Decide whether an array can be split into two subsets with equal sums.
edge_cases: An odd total is impossible
iterate sums from high to low so each number is used once
google_follow_up: Split into K subsets with equal sums instead.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
key_pattern: Track the running max and min product (a negative swaps them)
key_insight: A negative can turn the smallest product into the largest, so track both the max and min ending here.
statement: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest product.
edge_cases: A zero resets the run
a negative number swaps the max and min
google_follow_up: Return the subarray itself and handle products that overflow 64 bits.

title: Coin Change
key_pattern: Unbounded knapsack, min coins
key_insight: min coins for amount a = 1 + the min over coins of min coins for a - coin.
statement: Find the fewest coins needed to make an amount, or -1.
edge_cases: Amount 0 returns 0
unreachable amounts
google_follow_up: Count the number of ways instead (Coin Change II). Loop order?

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
key_pattern: Patience sorting tails + binary search
key_insight: Keep the smallest possible tail for every length; binary search where each number goes.
statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
edge_cases: Equal values do not extend the sequence
google_follow_up: Reconstruct one LIS; count all LIS.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
key_pattern: 2D DP on prefixes
key_insight: If the last characters match, extend the LCS of both shorter prefixes; otherwise drop one character from either side.
statement: Return the length of the longest common subsequence of two strings.
edge_cases: No common characters returns 0
google_follow_up: Diff two 1GB files: what changes (Hirschberg / Myers)?

title: Edit Distance
key_pattern: 2D DP over prefixes
key_insight: Each cell is the cheapest of insert, delete or replace applied to the shorter prefixes.
statement: Find the minimum insert/delete/replace operations to convert one word into another.
edge_cases: One string empty
google_follow_up: Reconstruct the actual edit script.

title: Split Array Largest Sum
key_pattern: Binary search on the answer with a greedy feasibility check (DP also works)
key_insight: If a max part sum S is feasible, any larger S is too, so binary search S and greedily count parts.
statement: Split an array into k non-empty contiguous parts so that the largest part sum is as small as possible.
edge_cases: k == len(nums) gives max(nums)
k == 1 gives the total
google_follow_up: The array is a stream of 10^9 numbers: approximate the split with bounded memory.

title: Trapping Rain Water
key_pattern: Monotonic decreasing stack of bars (or two pointers with running max)
key_insight: Water above a bar = min(tallest bar to its left, tallest to its right) - its height; prefix maxima or two pointers compute it.
statement: Compute how much rain water is trapped between bars of given heights.
edge_cases: Fewer than 3 bars traps nothing
google_follow_up: What about the 2D version (Trapping Rain Water II)?

title: Regular Expression Matching
key_pattern: 2D DP on text/pattern prefixes
key_insight: x* either matches nothing (skip the pair) or one more character (consume text, keep the pair).
statement: Implement regex matching with '.' and '*' covering the entire string.
edge_cases: Patterns like 'a*' matching empty
leading '*' is invalid
google_follow_up: Add '+' and '?' operators.

title: Burst Balloons
key_pattern: Interval DP: choose the last balloon to burst
key_insight: Pick the balloon burst last in a range: its neighbours are then the range's fixed borders, so the halves are independent.
statement: Burst balloons to maximise coins where bursting i gives nums[left]*nums[i]*nums[right].
edge_cases: Pad with 1 on both ends
google_follow_up: Why does choosing the first balloon to burst not work?

title: Daily Temperatures
key_pattern: Monotonic decreasing stack of indices
key_insight: Unresolved days wait on a decreasing stack; a warmer day resolves every colder day on top.
statement: For each day, return how many days you must wait until a warmer temperature (0 if never).
edge_cases: Equal temperatures do not count as warmer
google_follow_up: What if the series is a live feed and answers can be emitted late?

title: Next Greater Element II
key_pattern: Monotonic decreasing stack of indices over two passes (circular)
key_insight: For a circular array, run the monotonic stack over the indices twice (i mod n).
statement: For each element of a circular array, return the next greater element, or -1.
edge_cases: All-equal values return -1 everywhere
only push indices in the first pass
google_follow_up: Values stream in forever: emit each answer as soon as it is known.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
key_pattern: Monotonic increasing stack with sentinel
key_insight: A bar's widest rectangle reaches the nearest shorter bar on each side, found when the bar is popped from an increasing stack.
statement: Given bar heights of a histogram, find the area of the largest rectangle.
edge_cases: All equal heights
strictly increasing heights (flush the stack at the end)
google_follow_up: How does this extend to the maximal rectangle of 1s in a binary matrix?

title: Sliding Window Maximum
key_pattern: Monotonic deque of indices
key_insight: A decreasing deque drops values that can never be a window maximum again; its front is the current maximum.
statement: Return the maximum of every contiguous window of size k.
edge_cases: k == 1 and k == n
evict indices that fall out of the window
google_follow_up: What if you also need the median of every window?

title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
key_pattern: Prefix sums + monotonic increasing deque of indices
key_insight: On prefix sums, an increasing deque of start indices: pop the front while the sum reaches k, pop the back when a smaller prefix arrives.
statement: Return the length of the shortest non-empty subarray whose sum is at least k, or -1. Values can be negative.
edge_cases: Negatives break a plain sliding window
drop deque tails whose prefix sum is not smaller
google_follow_up: Answer it for 10^5 different values of k.

title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
key_pattern: Monotonic decreasing stack scanned right to left
key_insight: Right to left with a decreasing stack: each person sees everyone shorter they pop, plus the next taller person if there is one.
statement: People stand in a line with distinct heights. For each person, count how many people to their right they can see over everyone in between.
edge_cases: You see the first taller person, but nobody behind them
google_follow_up: People join and leave the queue: answer visibility queries quickly.
